messages.author: eafa26121223327e
messages.subject: inla.posterior.sample and quartiles
parts:
Hi All,

I'm hoping to gain some input about developing predictions using inla.posterior.sample. I am developing predictions for points across a region and across a period of ten years. There are about 686,702 data points in the region per year. The model I'm basing the posterior sampling on looks like the following:

Fixed effects:
                 mean    sd       0.025 quant    0.5 quant    0.975 quant  mode  kld
Intercept  5.275 0.075      5.128                 5.275             5.423      5.275   0
pond.std  0.314 0.001      0.312                 0.314             0.317     0.314    0

Random effects:
  Name    Model
    w SPDE2 model
   w.group AR1 model

Model hyperparameters:
                                                                                                 mean     sd        0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode
Range for w                                                                            78.012  3.583    69.437       77.774   87.839        77.176
Stdev for w                                                                             0.749    0.021      0.711        0.748        0.792          0.746
Precision for w.group                                                            108.209 47.584     40.297  100.262    222.937       84.411
Rho for w.group                                                                     0.227    0.250     -0.252    0.225      0.696            0.189

Expected number of effective parameters(stdev): 867.75(0.00)
Number of equivalent replicates : 7.70 

Watanabe-Akaike information criterion (WAIC) ...: 475609.87
Effective number of parameters .................: 48867.47

Marginal log-Likelihood:  -214227.22 
CPO and PIT are computed

Posterior marginals for the linear predictor and
 the fitted values are computed 

With the formula looking like:
formf= y ~  -1 + Intercept +pond.std+
 f(w, model=spde, hyper=hyperspde1)+f(w.group, model="ar1", hyper=hyper.ar1)
_______________________________________________________________________________________________

The model correlates well with the holdout data-set I kept back for testing fit (0.78 Spearman correlation)
However, when I run the following code (see below) on inla.posterior.sample (n=10000) modified from Fuglstad and Beguin 2017, the upper and lower quantiles seem excessively wide, running consistently from in the area of 40 -60 birds as a lower quantile, to a median of 150 - 350, with an upper quantile anywhere from 450 - 800 or 900. 

Am I missing something really obvious in the model output that's causing this? Or is my code below tripping up somewhere? What would you suggest moving forward?

Thanks again,
KK

NSim<-10000
simdata <- inla.posterior.sample(n = NSim, result = IG)
inn<-read.csv(".../PairInputData.csv")

#Select out 2008 data and develop predictions on that dataset
in8<-inn[inn$year==2008,]
in8$pond.std<-MyStd(in8$pond) #function to standardize covariate

Xp<-data.frame(Intercept=rep(1,nrow(in8)),pond.std=in8$pond.std)
Xm<-as.matrix(Xp)

Groupp <- in8$yr - 2007
table(Groupp)


tcoo3<-as.data.frame(cbind(in8$x,in8$y))
tcoo2 <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(tcoo3,tcoo3,proj4string = crs.m)   
tcoo<-spTransform(tcoo2,crs.km)

A_pred<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh=mesh,
loc=tcoo,
group = Groupp)

# Indices for different effects
idxSpace= IG$misc$configs$contents$start[3]
idxTime=IG$misc$configs$contents$start[4]
betaIndex<-which(IG$misc$configs$contents$length==1)
idxX= IG$misc$configs$contents$start[betaIndex]

#Covariates
xLatent = matrix(0, nrow = length(simdata[[1]]$latent), ncol = NSim)
        for(i in 1:NSim){
            xLatent[,i] = simdata[[i]]$latent
        }

xSpace = xLatent[idxSpace:(idxSpace+mesh$n-1),]
xX = xLatent[idxX,]
xTime08 = (xLatent[idxTime,])

quant = matrix(0, nrow = 3, ncol = nrow(Xm))


nBatch = 200
      brks = floor(seq(0, nrow(Xp), length.out = nBatch+1))
        for(batch in 1:nBatch){
            print(batch)
            
            # Extract idxs
            sIdx = brks[batch]+1
            eIdx = brks[batch+1]
            y<-matrix(0,nrow=length(sIdx:eIdx),ncol=NSim)
            # Get samples for current batch
            lambda= as.matrix(A_pred[sIdx:eIdx,]%*%xSpace1 + Xm[sIdx:eIdx,]%*%xX+xTime08) #Each column is a simulation so each row represents a location. 
           # Extract quantiles
  lambda2=exp(lambda)
for (j in 1:1000){
y[,j]<-rzipois(length(sIdx:eIdx),lambda=lambda2[,j],pstr0=simdata[[1]]$hyperpar[[1]])
}
  quant[, sIdx:eIdx] = apply(X = y, MARGIN = 1, FUN = quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
}

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample and quartiles
parts:
Hi,

I cc Geir-Arne in here, maybe he has comments as well, as its based on
this code.

Be aware, that a CI for the response come with 'double uncertainty',
first you have the uncertainty for the poisson response itself, which
is about sqrt(mean), so if the mean is 100, then you're looking at an
interval of about [80,120]. THEN, the mean itself is also uncertain,
say with stdev=10 around 100, then you're looking at a CI of about
[70,130]

H
